headline: Net loss widens on licensing comp, product sales ramp
summary_short: Ionis reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $267.9M (-40.7% y/y) as R&D/licensing revenue fell off a year-ago $280M Ono Pharmaceutical upfront payment, while commercial revenue rose 15% on DAWNZERA's launch; the net loss widened to $114.6M ($0.69/diluted share) from a $123.6M profit a year ago.
summary_long: Total revenue fell 40.7% y/y to $267.9M, driven by a licensing-revenue comparison: R&D/collaboration revenue dropped because the year-ago quarter included a $280M Ono Pharmaceutical upfront payment for sapablursen, partly offset by other partner milestone payments. Commercial revenue grew 15% y/y to $118.6M as DAWNZERA sales ramped following its August 2025 launch. Operating expenses (ex-equity comp) rose on SG&A investment behind TRYNGOLZA/DAWNZERA commercialization and zilganersen launch prep, pushing operating income to a $102.3M loss from a $139.8M profit. Net loss reached $114.6M ($0.69/diluted share) versus a $123.6M profit a year ago. Cash rose to $350.1M from $173.4M q/q after the April repayment of the 0% Notes due 2026, with short-term investments roughly steady at $1.70B. No numeric forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Company states net income fluctuations were driven by the revenue and expense factors discussed in the sections above: the licensing-revenue comparison, SG&A investment, and lower investment income.
R&D revenue fell because Q2 2025 included a $280M Ono Pharmaceutical upfront payment for sapablursen, partly offset by other partner milestones; commercial revenue rose 15% on DAWNZERA product sales.
Tracks the revenue decline plus SG&A growth from TRYNGOLZA/DAWNZERA commercialization investment and zilganersen launch prep, which the company says will keep rising through the rest of 2026.
Company attributes the swing to a loss to the revenue and operating-expense factors discussed above, plus lower investment income from a smaller average cash balance.
Tracks the net-income swing to a loss; diluted share count fell to 165.4M from 182.3M y/y, so per-share loss reflects the income swing on a smaller share base.
Not directly explained in the release; short-term investments were roughly flat q/q while cash rose, consistent with a portfolio mix shift following the April 2026 repayment of the 0% Notes due 2026.
Company states expenses have generally exceeded revenue since inception; accumulated deficit reached about $2.8B as of June 30, 2026, driving stockholders' equity down to about $0.4B.
